counting.name: Frequency Counting & Overwrite
counting.technique: Two passes: First pass counts frequencies of 0, 1, and 2. Second pass overwrites the original array with the counted number of 0s, then 1s, then 2s.
counting.teaches: Demonstrates that with a fixed small range of values (0, 1, 2), comparison sort O(n log n) is unnecessary, achieving O(n) with 3 counters. However, it requires two full passes over the array.

optimal.name: Dutch National Flag (Three Pointers)
optimal.technique: Single pass: Maintain 3 pointers (low, mid, high) dividing the array into 4 invariant regions: [0..low-1] confirmed 0s, [low..mid-1] confirmed 1s, [mid..high] unclassified/unknown, [high+1..n-1] confirmed 2s. Process nums[mid]: if 0 swap(low, mid) and increment both; if 1 increment mid; if 2 swap(mid, high) and decrement high without incrementing mid.
optimal.teaches: Teaches the fundamental 3-way partitioning invariant. Viscerally explains why mid must NOT advance when swapping with high (uninspected incoming value) and how maintaining clear boundary invariants guarantees single-pass in-place classification.

decision_reasoning.D1_brute_teaches_why: Counting approach clearly solves in O(n) time and O(1) space, but natural interview follow-up specifically asks for a single pass. It sets up the exact question: can we classify elements in-place the moment we encounter them?
decision_reasoning.D2_better_distinct: Dutch National Flag (DNF) provides the definitive single-pass three-pointer partition invariant, directly addressing the follow-up.
decision_reasoning.D4_data_structure_problem: In-place array manipulation and multi-pointer invariant maintenance.
decision_reasoning.D5_fewer_is_better: Two clean approaches (Counting 2-pass → Dutch National Flag 1-pass) perfectly structure the 10-scene narrative without unnecessary filler.
